builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Repository-Context-Guided Image Understanding for Agentic Software Development
summary: The method replaces direct VLM reading or OCR of degraded user screenshots by augmenting the coding agent with crisp screenshots rendered from the repository under modification, requiring no bug-free version or manual annotation. Costs include a rendering pipeline for reproducible application states (build, launch, screenshot automation), additional image tokens in the context, and infrastructure to keep rendered states current with the repository. It can fail when the application cannot be rendered automatically, when the bug manifests only under user-specific state absent from the rendered reference, or when the injected-bug benchmark does not transfer to real bug reports.
rationale: The approach is cheap to prototype on constrained infrastructure since it needs only repository rendering and existing VLM APIs, but the single-application benchmark and controlled degradation mean gains must be validated on the reader's own codebase and bug-report distribution before production adoption.
technique: Repository-rendered reference images for UI bug localization

claims.statement: The method replaces direct VLM reading or OCR of degraded user screenshots by augmenting the coding agent with crisp screenshots rendered from the repository under modification, requiring no bug-free version or manual annotation. Costs include a rendering pipeline for reproducible application states (build, launch, screenshot automation), additional image tokens in the context, and infrastructure to keep rendered states current with the repository. It can fail when the application cannot be rendered automatically, when the bug manifests only under user-specific state absent from the rendered reference, or when the injected-bug benchmark does not transfer to real bug reports.

Reference images raise gold-file match rate under fourfold downsampling with JPEG compression, and improve text recognition by approximately 12 percentage points over language-biased OCR at the same degradation level.
